design.unit: two admitted action edges converging on one exact written destination node
design.contrast: one shared result/state versus two independent results coincidentally written at one destination
design.prediction: A held fan-out should preserve one destination state and constrain both incoming actions to the same result class; an independent-output model predicts separable destination behavior when one incoming action changes.
design.countermodel: The same destination may be a repeated notation or editor-compressed location with no shared semantic result.
design.falsifier: Independent destination/state coding shows the two incoming actions require distinct results, or a matched fan-out has no shared downstream state constraint.
design.principal_risk: Current destination/result labels are working readings and no separately named final result is admitted.
design.related: Near GDT697/GDT701/GDT702, but targets the semantic consequence of fan-out topology rather than merely composing or counting relation edges.

source_evidence.quote:
The atlas now gives one exact home to every current edge.  Seven components
contain one edge, M006 is a two-action fan-out to one written destination, and
M007 is the sole serial chain with a written intermediate product.  The last
action in every component still lacks an admitted, separately named final
result.
